rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track;

SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY Country;
rows.note: Assuming "country" refers to Customer.Country, with customers having a NULL country grouped together.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS Year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS TotalRevenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assumption: total revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS TotalSpent FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assuming "total amount spent" means the sum of Invoice.Total per customer, I'll group by customer and return the top 5.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount FROM Employee e JOIN Customer c ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId GROUP BY e.EmployeeId ORDER BY CustomerCount DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assumption: "support rep" means Employee linked via Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll return only the top employee(s) by customer count, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS TrackCount FROM PlaylistTrack pt JOIN Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM Track WHERE TrackId NOT IN (SELECT TrackId FROM InvoiceLine WHERE TrackId IS NOT NULL);
rows.note: Assuming "never purchased" means the track does not appear in any InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'll sum invoice totals by BillingCountry for 2012 and return the top country.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.Name FROM Artist ar JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3 ORDER BY ar.Name LIMIT 50

SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM InvoiceLine il
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) DESC;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is `UnitPrice * Quantity` from InvoiceLine, and each genre's share is taken over total revenue across all invoice lines.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM Invoice i
JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM Invoice i2
  JOIN InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: Assuming "bought" means the customer appears on an invoice containing a track of that genre, I'll count customers with a Rock purchase and no Jazz purchase.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Month, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY Month ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming invoice revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar month for invoices dated in 2011.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId);
rows.note: Assumption: "full name" means FirstName and LastName from the Employee table, and employees with no customer whose SupportRepId points to them.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_date
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS f
WHERE first_date >= '2010-01-01' AND first_date < '2011-01-01';
rows.note: Assumption: a customer's first purchase is their earliest invoice date, and I count customers whose earliest invoice falls in 2010.

rows.sql: SELECT Album.Title, ROUND(SUM(Track.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS Minutes FROM Album JOIN Track ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId GROUP BY Album.AlbumId, Album.Title ORDER BY SUM(Track.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of Track.Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS Year,
         ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY Year
)
SELECT Year,
       Revenue,
       ROUND((Revenue - LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year)) * 100.0 / LAG(Revenue) OVER (ORDER BY Year), 1) AS PctChange
FROM yearly
ORDER BY Year
LIMIT 50;
rows.note: I'm assuming "invoice revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` per calendar year of `InvoiceDate`.

rows.sql:
WITH cust AS (
  SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spend
  FROM Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_average
FROM cust
WHERE spend > (SELECT AVG(spend) FROM cust);
rows.note: I'll treat each customer's spend as the sum of their invoice totals, and the average as the mean of those per-customer sums across customers who have invoices.

rows.sql:
WITH cnt AS (
  SELECT p.Name AS PlaylistName, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS ArtistCount
  FROM Playlist p
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.PlaylistId = p.PlaylistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
)
SELECT PlaylistName, ArtistCount
FROM cnt
WHERE ArtistCount = (SELECT MAX(ArtistCount) FROM cnt);
rows.note: Assumption: "largest number of distinct artists" counts distinct Artist rows reached via Track → Album → Artist for each playlist; ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) AS x
rows.note: Assumption: an invoice counts if its InvoiceLine rows reference tracks with at least two distinct GenreIds.

rows.sql:
WITH rep_rev AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS RepName, SUM(i.Total) AS Revenue
  FROM Invoice i
  JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
  JOIN Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
  WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, RepName
)
SELECT RepName, ROUND(Revenue, 2) AS Revenue
FROM rep_rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rep_rev);
rows.note: I'll assume "revenue" means the sum of `Invoice.Total` for 2010 invoices, grouped by each customer's support rep, and return the top rep (with ties included).

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year, g.Name AS Genre, SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
  GROUP BY Year, Genre
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rk
  FROM rev
)
SELECT Year, Genre, Revenue FROM ranked WHERE rk = 2 ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue is UnitPrice × Quantity from InvoiceLine, grouped by the invoice year, and that tied genres at second place are all shown.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_2013_than_2012
FROM (
  SELECT c.CustomerId,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2013,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2012
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
) t
WHERE total_2013 > total_2012;
rows.note: I'm treating a customer with no 2012 invoices as having spent 0 that year, and comparing the summed `Total` of invoices by year.

rows.sql: SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total FROM (SELECT Total FROM Invoice ORDER BY Total LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) - 1) / 2)
rows.note: Assuming the median is taken over all invoices' Total values (average of the two middle values if the count is even).

rows.sql:
WITH artist_playlists AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
  FROM Artist ar
  JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT ArtistId, Name, PlaylistCount
FROM artist_playlists
WHERE PlaylistCount = (SELECT MAX(PlaylistCount) FROM artist_playlists);
rows.note: I'm counting each artist's distinct playlists through Track → Album → Artist, and returning all artists tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(il.InvoiceLineId) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT i.InvoiceId), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice FROM Invoice i LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId;
rows.note: Assumption: average line items = total InvoiceLine rows divided by number of distinct invoices (invoices with no lines count as zero).

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '1'
rows.note: Assuming Discontinued = '1' marks a discontinued product.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany';

SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM Categories c JOIN Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName HAVING COUNT(p.ProductID) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Products GROUP BY CategoryID))
rows.note: Assuming "most products" means the count of rows in Products per CategoryID, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by calendar year.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS AverageFreight FROM Orders o JOIN Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assuming "average freight per shipper" means grouping Orders by ShipVia and joining to Shippers for the company name.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: Assuming Andrew Fuller is the employee with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller', I'll find his subordinates via ReportsTo.

rows.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Orders o JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY e.EmployeeID) SELECT name, n AS order_count FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c);
rows.note: I'll count orders by `EmployeeID` where `OrderDate` falls in 2020, then return the employee(s) with the highest count, including ties.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the mean of Products.UnitPrice across all products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped_to_france FROM Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France';
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' in the Orders table, counting all orders regardless of whether ShippedDate is filled in.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS Revenue FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 5;
rows.note: Assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from "Order Details", summed per product, and joined to Products for the name.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice
FROM Products p
JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
WHERE p.UnitPrice = (
  SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID
)
ORDER BY c.CategoryName;
rows.note: I'm assuming "most expensive" means the highest `Products.UnitPrice` within each category, and I'll include all products tied for that price.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.CustomerID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2021-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2022-01-01'
  GROUP BY o.CustomerID
)
SELECT c.CompanyName, r.revenue
FROM rev r
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: I'll treat revenue as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over order lines, using orders dated in 2021, and return all customers tied for the top total.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM Orders WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assuming "orders" means rows in Orders by OrderDate year 2021, grouped by calendar month.

rows.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
)
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, OrderCount
FROM counts
WHERE OrderCount = (SELECT MAX(OrderCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: The database has no orders from 1997. Order dates run from 2012-07-10 to 2023-10-28, and a count of orders dated in 1997 returned 0. The question can't be answered from this data.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped after their required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days_to_ship FROM Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL;
rows.note: Assuming "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between OrderDate and ShippedDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql:
SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Orders o
JOIN Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019'
GROUP BY c.Country
HAVING COUNT(o.OrderID) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(o2.OrderID) AS cnt
    FROM Orders o2
    JOIN Customers c2 ON c2.CustomerID = o2.CustomerID
    WHERE strftime('%Y', o2.OrderDate) = '2019'
    GROUP BY c2.Country
  )
);
rows.note: I'm assuming "customers from which country" means the country on the customer record (Customers.Country), and that orders are counted by OrderDate in 2019.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS BeveragesPercentage FROM "Order Details" od JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2023';
rows.note: I'm treating revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from "Order Details", using orders whose OrderDate falls in 2023.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12) t;
rows.note: I'll count customers who have orders in each of the 12 months of 2020 (distinct months from OrderDate).

rows.sql:
WITH order_values AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_values
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
WHERE ea.avg_order_value = (SELECT MAX(avg_order_value) FROM emp_avg);
rows.note: I'll compute each order's value as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) across its lines, average those per employee, and return the top employee (all tied rows if there is a tie).

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT s.CompanyName AS SupplierName,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS Revenue
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID
  JOIN Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018'
  GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName
)
SELECT SupplierName, Revenue
FROM rev
WHERE Revenue = (SELECT MAX(Revenue) FROM rev);
rows.note: I'm assuming revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from Order Details, with 2018 based on OrderDate.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT y.ProductID, p.ProductName, y.units_2021, y.units_2022,
         y.units_2022 - y.units_2021 AS increase
  FROM yearly y
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = y.ProductID
)
SELECT ProductID, ProductName, units_2021, units_2022, increase
FROM diff
WHERE increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM diff);
rows.note: I'll treat "units sold" as the sum of `Quantity` from Order Details by order year (`OrderDate`), and the increase as 2022 units minus 2021 units in absolute terms.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "late" means ShippedDate is later than RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT yr AS Year, SUM(cnt) OVER (ORDER BY yr ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CumulativeOrders FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Orders GROUP BY yr) ORDER BY yr
rows.note: Assuming "year" is the year of OrderDate and the cumulative count runs across years in ascending order:

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM (SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total FROM "Order Details" GROUP BY OrderID HAVING total > 10000) AS t
rows.note: I'll compute each order's total as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its line items, then count orders above 10,000.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) AS yr,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) IN ('2018', '2019')
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID, yr
),
diff AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2018' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2019' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev_2019,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2019' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN yr = '2018' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS growth
  FROM yearly
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS employee_name,
       d.rev_2018, d.rev_2019, d.growth
FROM diff d
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = d.EmployeeID
ORDER BY d.growth DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll compute each employee's after-discount revenue (UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) by order year, then take the employee with the largest 2019 minus 2018 increase.
